  "text": "Beside the bowl lay his schoolbag.

Not the one hanging in the hall. This one was new, its buckle bright, the tear beneath the strap not yet made.

“That was Tuesday,” the boy said.

His father closed his eyes.

On Tuesday, three winters ago, the boy had missed the bus. His mother had driven him. There had been ice by the bridge, though the road outside their house was clear.

The man behind the wall pulled out a chair.

“You can still sit down,” he said.

Anne emerged holding a wooden box. Inside were keys arranged on wool, each with a paper label tied to its stem. The boy saw his name on several.

“What does he do?” he asked her.

“He keeps the mornings open.”

“All of them?”

“Only the ones your father pays for.”

His father lifted his hand from the floor. A pale print remained on the boards, and slowly faded.

The boy looked through the crack again. Beyond the table stood a blue coat, hanging from the back of a chair. One sleeve had been turned inside out. His mother always left it that way, then complained when she dressed in a hurry.

“Where is she?”

“Upstairs,” said the man.

His father reached for him, but stopped short of touching his wrist.

“If you go in, someone has to come out.”

“Her?”

“No.”

At the table, the other man leaned into view. He had his father's face, but his hands were smooth and unmarked.

From upstairs came the brief cough of a woman waking.

The boy turned the key another quarter."
